la:noun:argumentum.gloss: argument (as in an argument for a position); evidence, a proof
senses: argument (as in an argument for a position); evidence, a proof
la:noun:argumentum.html:
argūmentum, i, n.
arguo
.
The means by which an assertion or assumption may be made clear, proved, an argument, evidence, proof (and in particular, that which rests upon facts, while ratio is that which depends upon reasoning): argumentum est ratio, quae rei dubiae facit fidem,: quid est argumentum? Probabile inventum ad faciendam fidem, : argumentum est ratio probationem praestans, quā colligitur aliquid per aliud, et quae, quod est dubium, per id quod dubium non est, confirmat,: de eā re signa atque argumenta paucis verbis eloquar,; ; ; : commemorando Argumenta fidem dictis conradere,; so : argumenta multa et firma ad probandum,: aliquid exemplis magis quam argumentis refellere,: argumento esse,; : litterae ad senatum missae argumentum fuere, etc.,: In argumentum fidei retentum pallium ostendit marito,; : inopia fecerat eam (rem parvam) argumentum ingens caritatis,: libertatis argumentum,: Est fides argumentum non apparentium,: addit pro argumento,: velut argumentum rursus conditae urbis,: levibus utrimque argumentis, et saep.—
A sign by which any thing is known, a mark, token, evidence: animi laeti Argumenta,signs, indications,: voti potentis,: unguentarii myrrham digerunt haud difficulter odoris atque pinguetudinis argumentis, according to the indications of smell, etc., : caelum quidem haud dubie caelati argumenti dicimus,: amoris hoc est argumentum, non malignitatis,: argumenta viri, i. e. indicia,—
The matter which lies at the basis of any written or artistic representation, contents, subject, theme, argument, ὑπόθεσις: Argumentum plura significat. Nam et fabulae ad actum scaenicarum compositae argumenta dicuntur: et orationum Ciceronis velut thema ipse exponens Pedianus, argumentum, inquit, tale est: quo apparet omnem ad scribendum destinatam materiam ita appellari, and 10.
Of every kind of representation in writing.
Lit.: argumentum est ficta res, quae tamen fieri potuit,; : tabulae novae, quid habent argumenti, nisi ut, etc.,what is their drift? what do they mean?: epistulae,; ; .
But esp. freq., the subject-matter of a poem or fictitious writing, the subject, contents: post argumentum hujus eloquar tragoediae,; cf. ; so : argumentum narrare,: fabulae,: Livius Andronicus ab saturis ausus est primus argumento fabulam serere,i. e. a scenic representation of a subject in its connection,: spectaculum, quo argumenta inferorum explicarentur,.—Hence,
Meton. (part for the whole), a poem in gen.: explicare argumenti exitum,: hoc argumento se describi sentiat,; so ; ; cf. Enn. ap. : sumque argumenti conditor ipse mei,I am myself the subject of my poem,.—
Trop., intrinsic worth, reality, truth: haec tota fabella ... quam est sine argumento,without value, reality,: non sine argumento maledicere,not without some reason,fin.—
The subject of artistic representations (sculpture, painting, embroidery. etc.): ex ebore diligentissime perfecta argumenta erant in valvis,: (cratera) fabricaverat Alcon Hyleus, et longo caelaverat argumento,; cf. sq.: vetus in telā deducitur argumentum,; : Parrhasii tabulae,.— In philos. lang., a conclusion, a syllogism: Nam concludi non potest nisi iis, quae ad concludendum sumpta erunt, ita probatis ut falsa ejusdem modi nulla possint esse,

la:noun:argentum.html:
argentum, i, n.
ἀργήεις, ἀργής, Dor. ἀργᾶς, white, like Tarentum, from Τάρας, Doed. Syn. III. p. 193; prop. white metal; cf. Sanscr. arǵunas = bright; raǵatam = silver; hence
,
silver, whose mineralogical description is found in .
Lit.: argenti metalla,: argenti aerisque metalla,: argenti vena,: argenti fodina, v. argenti-fodina; argenti scoria,: spuma argenti,: argenti duae differentiae (sunt),: argentum candidum, rufum, nigrum,: argentum infectum,unwrought silver,; : argenti montes,: argentum purum, Foedus ap. : argento circumcludere cornua,: Concisum argentum in titulos faciesque minutas,: quod usquam est Auri atque argenti,: argentum et aurum,; , ; : aurum argentumque,. 82: aurum et argentum,.—
Meton.
Wrought silver, things made of silver; silver-plate, silver-work: tu argentum eluito,: nec domus argento fulget auroque renidet,; so, ridet argento domus,: argenti quod erat solis fulgebat in armis,: argentumque expositum in aedibus,: navis plena argenti facti atque signati,full of wrought and stamped silver,; so and 26: argentum caelatum,; : apponitur cena in argento puro et antiquo,: argentum et marmor vetus aeraque et artīs Suspice,; so ; 2, 2, 181; : argenti vascula puri,; : vasa omnia ex argento,; : leve argentum,: argentum paternum,: argentum vetus,: argentum mittere,: Empturus pueros, argentum, murrina, villas, et saep.—
Silver as weighed out for money, or money coined from silver, silver, silver money; and, as the most current coin, for money in gen.: appendit pecuniam, quadringentos siclos argenti,: Ratio quidem hercle adparet; argentum οἴχεται, (quoted by Cic., Pis. 25 fin.): expetere,: adnumerare,; so ; ; ; : argenti sitis famesque,; : quis audet Argento praeferre caput,: tenue argentum venaeque secundae,: hic modium argenti,: venter Argenti gravis capax,: Argentum et aurum non est mihi,; et saep.—
Argentum vivum, quicksilver, ; sqq.; so, argentum liquidum,.

Somewhat subtle, acute, keen (v. argutus, B. 1.): libri,.

la:verb:argumentor.gloss: to adduce arguments or proof of something, prove, reason
senses: to adduce arguments or proof of something, prove, reason
to adduce something as an argument or proof
la:verb:argumentor.html:
argūmentor, ātus, 1, v. dep.
argumentum
.
To adduce proof of a thing, to prove: ego neque in causis, si quid est evidens, de quo inter omnes conveniat, argumentari soleo,; ; : cum essem argumentatus,; —
To adduce something as proof: atque ego illa non argumentabor, quae sunt gravia vehementer, eum corrupisse, etc.,: multa,.—
To make a conclusion, to conclude: de voluntate alicujus,; cf. Auct. ad .!*? Pass.: omnia argumentata nomina πιστωθέντα, Aufusius ap. P.

la:adj:argenteus.html:
argentĕus, a, um, adj.
argentum
.
Of or from silver, made of silver (cf. argentum, I. A.): polubrum, Liv. And. ap. : aquila,: brattea,: phalerae,: vasa,; so ; ; : Triton,: dei,: leones,: simulacra,: nummus,; so : denarius,; also absol. argenteus, ; so ; —
Metaph.
Adorned with silver, = argentatus: scaena,: acies, (cf. a little before: per picta atque aurata scuta; and v. argentatus, I.).—
Of a white, silver color, silvery: niveis argentea pennis Ales,: color,; so, fons,: undae,: lilia,: anser,: crinis,—
Of the silver age: subiit argentea proles, Auro deterior, fulvo pretiosior aere,.—
In comic style, of or from money (cf. argentum, I. B. 2.): salus,a silver salutation,: amica tua facta est argentea, is turned into money, i. e. has been sold, .

la:noun:argus.html:
Argus, i, m., = Ἄργος.
The hundred-eyed keeper of Io, after she was changed into a heifer by Jupiter; slain by Mercury at the bidding of Jupiter. His hundred eyes were placed by Juno in the tail of the peacock, ; ; (cf. Eustath. ad Hom. Il. 2, p. 138; Schol. ad Eurip. Phoen. v. 1123; Heyne, Apollod. p. 249 sq.).—
The builder of the ship Argo, and 314.—
Argus, a, um, adj., = Argivus; v. Argos, II. D.

la:other:Argos.html:
Argŏs, n. (only nom. and acc.), more freq. in the plur.Argi, ōrum, m. ( Müll.: Graecanice hoc Argos, cum Latine Argei; cf. Prob. p. 1447 P.; Phocae Ars, p. 1707 P.), = Ἄργος.
Argos, the capital of Argolis, in the Peloponnesus, sacred to Juno, also called Argos Hippium and Argos Dipsium or Inachium, ; ; cf. Mann. Gr. p. 641 sq.: quaerit Argos Amymonen,; so ; : securum per Argos,; so : patriis ab Argis Pellor,; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—The acc. Argos, occurring in the histt., is best considered as plur., since the sing. seems rather to belong to the poets and geographers (e. g. Plin. above cited); cf. Daehne and Bremi ad .—
Poet., Argos is sometimes put for the whole of Greece, .—Hence,
Derivv., the adjj.,
Argīvus, a, um (i. e. ArgiFus from ArgeiFos, like Achivus from Ἀχαιός), of Argos, Argive, : Argivus orator,: augur,i.e. Amphiaraus,

—An epithet of Juno (as in the Iliad Ἀργεία is an appel. of Here) as tutelary goddess of Argos, .—

Poet. for Greek or Grecian in gen.: castra,: phalanx,: ensis,: Thalia, (cf. : Graja Camena).—And so Argivi for the Greeks: classis Argivūm,; ; ; , ext. 4.—
Without digamma, Argēus (Argī-), a, um, Argive or Grecian: Argia sacerdos, (B. and K., Argiva): Tibur Argeo positum colono (cf. ), K. and H.; so, Tibur Argeum, Merk. —
Argŏlis, ĭdis, f., = Ἀργολίς.
Argive: Alcmene,: puppis,.—
Subst. (sc. terra), the province of Argolis, in Peloponnesus, prooem.; .—Hence, Argŏlĭ-cus, a, um, adj., = Ἀργολικός, Argolic: sinus,: mare,: urbes,: leo,the Nemean lion,—Also Grecian in gen.: duces,the Grecian leaders in the Trojan war,: classis, al.—*
Argus, a, um, adj., Argive: Argus pro Argivus, (prol. 98): Amphitruo natus Argis ex Argo patre,. (So the much-contested passage seems to be better explained than when, with Gronov. Observv. 4, 298, Argo is considered as abl. from Argos, begotten of a father from Argos, to which Argis in the plur. does not correspond.)

la:verb:arguo.gloss: to clarify, to make plain; to assert, declare, prove, show
senses: to clarify, to make plain; to assert, declare, prove, show
to argue, to allege; to disclose; to complain of, convict
la:verb:arguo.html:
argŭo, ŭi, ūtum (ŭĭtum, hence arguiturus, ap. P.), 3, v. a.
cf. ἀργής, white; ἀργός, bright; Sanscr. árgunas, bright; ragatas, white; and rag, to shine (v. argentum and argilla); after the same analogy we have clarus, bright; and claro, to make bright, to make evident; and the Engl. clear, adj., and to clear = to make clear; v.
.
In gen., to make clear, to show, prove, make known, declare, assert, μηνύειν: arguo Eam me vidisse intus,: non ex auditu arguo,: M. Valerius Laevinus ... speculatores, non legatos, venisse arguebat,: degeneres animos timor arguit,: amantem et languor et silentium Arguit,; .—Pass., in a mid. signif.: apparet virtus arguiturque malis,makes itself known,: laudibus arguitur vini vinosus Homerus,betrays himself,.—
Esp.
With aliquem, to attempt to show something, in one's case, against him, to accuse, reprove, censure, charge with: Indicāsse est detulisse; arguisse accusāsse et convicisse, (cf. : Argutum iri in discrimen vocari): tu delinquis, ego arguar pro malefactis? Enn. (as transl. of Eurip. Iphig. Aul. 384: Εἶτʼ ἐγὼ δίκην δῶ σῶν κακῶν ὁ μὴ σφαλείς) ap. Rufin. § 37: servos ipsos neque accuso neque arguo neque purgo,: Pergin, sceleste, intendere hanc arguere?; : hae tabellae te arguunt,: an hunc porro tactum sapor arguet oris?: quod adjeci, non ut arguerem, sed ne arguerer,: coram aliquem arguere,: apud praefectum,: (Deus) arguit te heri,; ; ; —
With the cause of complaint in the gen.; abl. with or without de; with in with abl.; with acc.; with a clause as object; or with ut (cf. Ramsh. p. 326; Zumpt, § 446).
With gen.: malorum facinorum, (cf. infra, argutus, B. 2.): aliquem probri, Stupri, dedecoris,: viros mortuos summi sceleris,: aliquem tanti facinoris,: criminis,: furti me arguent,; : repetundarum,: occupandae rei publicae,: neglegentiae,: noxae,: veneni in se comparati,: socordiae,: mendacii,: timoris,: sceleris arguemur,; —
With abl.: te hoc crimine non arguo,; —
With de: de eo crimine, quo de arguatur,: de quibus quoniam verbo arguit, etc.,: Quis arguet me de peccato?; .—
With in with abl. (eccl. Lat.): non in sacrificiis tuis arguam te,.—(ε) With acc.: quid undas Arguit et liquidam molem camposque natantīs? of what does he impeach the waves? etc., quid being here equivalent to cujus or de quo, Munro.—(ζ) With an inf.-clause as object: quae (mulier) me arguit Hanc domo ab se subripuisse,; : occidisse patrem Sex. Roscius arguitur,: auctor illius injuriae fuisse arguebatur?: qui sibimet vim ferro intulisse arguebatur,; ; : me Arguit incepto rerum accessisse labori,; .—(η) With ut, as in Gr. ὡς (post-Aug. and rare), : hunc ut dominum et tyrannum, illum ut proditorem arguentes,as being master and tyrant,.—
Transf. to the thing.
To accuse, censure, blame: ea culpa, quam arguo,: peccata coram omnibus argue,: tribuni plebis dum arguunt in C. Caesare regni voluntatem,; : taciturnitatem pudoremque quorumdam pro tristitiā et malignitate arguens,; : arguebat et perperam editos census,he accused of giving a false statement of property, census,: primusque animalia mensis Arguit imponi,censured, taught that it was wrong,: ut non arguantur opera ejus,.—
Trop., to denounce as false: quod et ipsum Fenestella arguit, Roth.—With reference to the person, to refute, confute: aliquem,.—Hence, argūtus, a, um, P. a.
Of physical objects, clear.
To the sight, bright, glancing, lively: manus autem minus arguta, digitis subsequens verba, non exprimens,not too much in motion, (cf. : nullae argutiae digitorum, and ,

119-123): manus inter agendum argutae admodum et gestuosae,: et oculi nimis arguti, quem ad modum animo affecti sumus, loquuntur,: ocelli,; : argutum caput,a head graceful in motion, (breve, Servius, but this idea is too prosaic): aures breves et argutae, ears that move quickly (not stiff, rigid), : argutā in soleā,in the neat sandal,.—

To the hearing, clear, penetrating, piercing, both of pleasant and disagreeable sounds, clear-sounding, sharp, noisy, rustling, whizzing, rattling, clashing, etc. (mostly poet.): linguae, Naev. ap. : aves,: hirundo,chirping,: olores,tuneful,: ilex, murmuring, rustling (as moved by the wind), : nemus, al.—Hence, a poet. epithet of the musician and poet, clear-sounding, melodious: Neaera,: poëtae,: fama est arguti Nemesis formosa Tibullus,: forum, full of bustle or din, noisy, : serra,grating,: pecten,rattling,; (cf. in Gr. κερκὶς ἀοιδός, Aristoph. Ranae, v. 1316) al.—Hence, of rattling, prating, verbose discourse: sine virtute argutum civem mihi habeam pro preaeficā, etc.,: [Neque mendaciloquom neque adeo argutum magis], Ritschl.—
Trop., of written communications, rattling, wordy, verbose: obviam mihi litteras quam argutissimas de omnibus rebus crebro mittas,: vereor, ne tibi nimium arguta haec sedulitas videatur, Cael. ap. . —Transf. to omens, clear, distinct, conclusive, clearly indicative, etc.: sunt qui vel argutissima haec exta esse dicant,: non tibi candidus argutum sternuit omen Amor?.—
To the smell; sharp, pungent: odor argutior,.—
To the taste; sharp, keen, pungent: sapor,; .—
Of mental qualities.
In a good sense, bright, acute, sagacious, witty: quis illo (sc. Catone) acerbior in vituperando? in sententiis argutior?: orator,: poëma facit ita festivum, ita concinnum, ita elegans, nihil ut fieri possit argutius,; so, dicta argutissima,: sententiae,: acumen,: arguto ficta dolore queri,dexterously-feigned pain,—
In a bad sense, sly, artful, cunning: meretrix,: calo. : milites,.—As a pun: ecquid argutus est? is he cunning? Ch. Malorum facinorum saepissime (i.e. has been accused of), (v. supra, I. B. a.).—Hence, adv.: argūtē (only in the signif. of B.).
Subtly, acutely: respondere,: conicere,: dicere,.—Comp.: dicere,.— Sup.: de re argutissime disputare,.—
Craftily: obrepere,; .

la:noun:argumentatio.html:
argūmentātĭo, ōnis, f.
argumentor
(a rhet. t. t., most freq. in Cic.).
An adducing of proof, an argumentation: argumentatio nomine uno res duas significat, ideo, quod et inventum aliquam in rem probabile aut necessarium, argumentatio vocatur et ejus inventi artificiosa expolitio,: argumentatio est explicatio argumenti,: perspicuitas argumentatione elevatur,: probabilis,: expositio verbosior quibusdam argumentis, argumentis dico, non argumentatione,; ; —
The proof itself: etiamne in tam perspicuis rebus argumentatio quaerenda est aut conjectura capienda?.

er or broker: M. Fulcinius, qui Romae argentariam non ignobilem fecit,: argentariā dissolutā,after the dissolution, closing up, of the bank,: exercere,: administrare,.—

Argo, ūs, f. (
gen. Argūs, ; acc. Argo, Varr. ap. P.; Argon, Prop 1, 20, 17 Müll.; dat. and abl. prob. not used), = Ἀργώ, the name of the ship in which the Greek heroes, under the guidance of Jason, sailed to Colchis in quest of the golden fleece, Enn. ap. Argo navis occidit: tempestatem significat, interdum pluviam,.—Acc. to the first signif., Argō-us, a, um, adj., = Ἀργῶος, pertaining to the Argo, and in gen. to the Argonauts, ; ; ; ; ; 8, 294.

white clay, potter's earth, argil; cf. ; : homulus ex argillā et luto fictus, * : glandes ferventes ex argillā fusili, * (ἐξ ἀργίλλης τετηγμένης, Paraphr.): idoneus arti Cuilibet, argillā quidvis imitabitur udā, * : Tenuis ubi argilla et dumosis calculus arvis, * .
